stage: author full-triple precision pass before final peer acceptance

rationale.before: Both state that David struck Moab and Moab became his servants bringing gifts; Samuel additionally gives two measured lengths killed and two kept alive, which are not replaced with a different ratio.
rationale.after: Both state that David struck Moab and Moab became his servants bringing gifts; Samuel additionally assigns two measured lengths to death and keeps two measured lengths alive, which are not replaced with a different ratio.

relationship.before: David's northern victory and the Euphrates-control clause in parallel accounts
relationship.after: David's victory and the Euphrates-control clause in parallel accounts

rationale.before: Both summaries describe David striking a northern king and mention establishing control at the Euphrates; Hadadezer son of Raab, Zobah and Adraazar, Souba, Hemath remain as supplied, without assigning the final he to a newly resolved actor.
rationale.after: Both summaries describe David striking a king and mention establishing control at the Euphrates; Hadadezer son of Raab, Zobah and Adraazar, Souba, Hemath remain as supplied, without assigning the final he to a newly resolved actor.

relationship.before: David's bronze spoil explicitly linked with Solomon's temple objects
relationship.after: David's bronze spoil explicitly linked with Solomon's bronze objects

rationale.before: David confirms the Saul-house servant's name Ziba; the next exchange has Ziba answer the question about a surviving member by naming Jonathan's injured son, rather than a newly inferred claimant.
rationale.after: The Saul-house servant is named Ziba and called before David; the next exchange has Ziba identify Jonathan's surviving son by parentage and injured feet, without giving that son's personal name in this exchange.

relationship.before: Same-chapter Ziba receives the implementation of the land-restoration promise
relationship.after: Same-chapter Ziba receives directions concerning the land-restoration promise

relationship.before: Ammon's retreat after Syrian flight with distinct named pursuing actors
relationship.after: Ammon's retreat after Syrian flight with distinct opposing-actor clauses

rationale.before: Both have Ammon see Syrian flight, enter the city and Joab return to Jerusalem; Samuel says they flee before Abishai, whereas Chronicles names Joab and Abessa, keeping those actual actor clauses intact.
rationale.after: Both report Ammon entering the city after seeing Syria flee and a return to Jerusalem; Samuel says they flee before Abishai, whereas Chronicles names Joab and Abessa, keeping those actual actor clauses intact.

relationship.before: Spring campaign, Rabbah siege and David remaining in Jerusalem
relationship.after: Royal campaign, Rabbah siege and David remaining in Jerusalem

rationale.before: David requests Uriah from Joab and Joab sends him; the next unit places Uriah with David answering questions about Joab, the people and the war, recording that particular request and arrival.
rationale.after: David requests Uriah from Joab and Joab sends him; the next unit says Uriah arrives and David asks about Joab, the people and the war, recording that particular summons and arrival without inventing Uriah's answers.

relationship.before: Same-chapter declared abstention continues after the king makes Uriah drunk
relationship.after: Same-chapter refusal to go home repeated after the royal meal

rationale.before: The letter orders Uriah placed in fierce fighting and withdrawal behind him; Joab's action places him among powerful defenders and the account reports his death, without adding an unreported description of every withdrawal manoeuvre.
rationale.after: The letter orders Uriah placed in fierce fighting and withdrawal behind him; Joab places him where he knows there are powerful men, and the account reports his death, without adding an unreported description of every withdrawal manoeuvre.

relationship.before: Same-chapter placement among powerful defenders followed by the city's attack
relationship.after: Same-chapter stated placement followed by the city's attack

rationale.before: David becomes angry and cites the wall danger and Abimelech after Joab prepared the messenger for those questions, preserving the actual Greek-edition response rather than omitting its repeated speech.
rationale.after: David becomes angry and cites the wall danger and Abimelech after Joab prepared the messenger for those questions, preserving the actual source-edition response rather than omitting its repeated speech.

rationale.before: David tells Joab not to regard the matter as evil and attributes varied losses to the sword; the chapter closes by saying David's act was evil in the Lord's eyes, preserving the explicit contrast between those evaluations.
rationale.after: David tells Joab not to regard the reported battle matter as evil and attributes varied losses to the sword; the chapter closes by calling what David had done evil in the Lord's eyes, contrasting the evil wording while retaining the broader scope of the concluding judgment.

relationship.before: Davidic confession directly addressed to God in narrative and psalm
relationship.after: David's sin-against-God confession in narrative and psalm

rationale.before: David confesses sin to Nathan's Lord-message; after the later census he tells the Lord he has sinned greatly and asks removal of lawlessness, preserving the different occasions and the distinct responses that follow.
rationale.after: David tells Nathan he has sinned against the Lord; after the later census he tells the Lord he has sinned greatly and asks removal of lawlessness, preserving the different addressees, occasions and responses that follow.
